articles.title: Como jovem nascido sem braços que conquistou CNH construiu autonomia | G1
articles.standfirst: Atendimentos na AACD e em APAEs, além do incentivo da família, fizeram parte da infância de Reiner Jesus Martins, que hoje mora sozinho e cursa agronomia em Lavras (MG).
articles.summary: Atendimentos na AACD e em APAEs, além do incentivo da família, fizeram parte da infância de Reiner Jesus Martins, que hoje mora sozinho e cursa agronomia em Lavras (MG).
articles.body:
Reiner Jesus Martins, de 20 anos, nasceu sem os dois braços e, desde os primeiros meses de vida, passou por terapias e acompanhamentos que ajudaram no desenvolvimento da autonomia. Hoje, estudante de agronomia da Universidade Federal de Lavras (UFLA), ele mora sozinho em Lavras (MG), dirige e compartilha nas redes sociais a rotina de quem aprendeu a fazer as atividades do dia a dia de uma maneira própria.

Natural de Juatuba, na Região Metropolitana de Belo Horizonte, Reiner conta que a mãe descobriu ainda durante a gravidez que ele nasceria sem os braços. A partir da descoberta, ela, que já tinha outros dois filhos, passou a buscar informações e instituições que pudessem ajudar no desenvolvimento e na criação do caçula.

Desde bebê, Reiner foi atendido por instituições como a Associação de Assistência à Criança Deficiente (AACD) e APAEs de diferentes cidades. Também fez terapia ocupacional, equoterapia e hidroterapia.

"A terapia é muito baseada na questão de te dar a forma para você encontrar a maneira de fazer as coisas", explica o estudante.

Como jovem nascido sem braços que conquistou CNH construiu autonomia ao longo da vida — Foto: Reiner Jesus Martins/Arquivo pessoal

Dentro de casa, o estímulo à independência também fazia parte da rotina. Segundo Reiner, a mãe sempre buscou ensiná-lo a realizar as tarefas sozinho, com a compreensão de que ela e outros familiares não estariam ao lado dele o tempo todo.

Foi assim que ele aprendeu a usar principalmente os pés para realizar atividades que normalmente são feitas com as mãos. Ele também utiliza a boca, o queixo e o tronco em algumas situações.

"Hoje, para mim, meus pés são como as mãos", conta o jovem.

Reiner descreve a infância como normal, apesar da rotina diferente de outras crianças. Ele estudava em escola pública e também precisava conciliar as aulas com os atendimentos.

Como a família morava em Juatuba e muitas terapias eram realizadas em Betim (MG), a mãe e o filho dependiam de ônibus para se deslocar. A rotina começava cedo e, em alguns dias, terminava apenas depois das aulas.

A família também buscava garantir que ele tivesse convivência com outras crianças, participasse das atividades escolares e desenvolvesse diferentes aspectos da vida.

Família foi essencial na construção da autonomia do jovem — Foto: Reiner Jesus Martins/Arquivo pessoal

A mãe teve papel central nesse processo. Ela deixou o emprego na área comercial de uma gráfica em Belo Horizonte quando descobriu a condição do filho e passou a se dedicar à criação dele. O pai continuou trabalhando.

Além dos pais, Reiner destaca o apoio dos irmãos, avós, padrinhos e outros familiares. Um dos exemplos foi o padrinho, que construiu uma bicicleta adaptada para ele quando ainda era criança.

O veículo não tinha um guidão convencional e permitia que Reiner conduzisse a bicicleta utilizando o tronco. Até hoje, a bicicleta é guardada pela família.

Bicicleta adaptada construída pelo padrinho de Reiner continua guardada — Foto: Reiner Jesus Martins/Arquivo pessoal

Ao longo da infância, Reiner aprendeu a escrever, comer, escovar os dentes e se vestir usando os pés. Para ele, muitas dessas habilidades foram adquiridas de maneira tão natural que nem consegue dizer exatamente quando aprendeu cada uma delas.

"O corpo meio que se adapta à realidade. Se ele não tem os braços, o corpo vai se adaptar da forma que tem", afirma.

A autonomia também foi construída diante de situações de preconceito e de pessoas que não sabiam como reagir à deficiência. Ele conta que, quando era criança, já foi chamado de "sem braço" por outras crianças. Em uma dessas situações, a orientação da mãe foi para que Reiner respondesse e tentasse conversar com o menino.

"Eu falei assim: 'Olha, tudo bem, eu sou sem braço, sim, mas meu nome é Reiner. E o seu? Você quer ser meu amigo?'"

Para ele, situações como essa ajudaram a aprender a lidar com olhares, perguntas e atitudes de pessoas que não estavam acostumadas a conviver com alguém com deficiência.

Reiner afirma que ainda enfrenta situações de capacitismo, quando as pessoas duvidam de sua capacidade de realizar determinadas atividades. "Eu provo para mim mesmo que eu consigo e, depois, eu vou e provo para as outras pessoas", conta.

Ao mesmo tempo, ele reconhece que há momentos em que gostaria de ter os braços. "Tem hora que eu xingo, reclamo, porque eu queria ter os braços. Queria viver como uma pessoa comum com os braços também."

Segundo ele, a forma encontrada para lidar com essa realidade foi valorizar o que consegue fazer e o apoio que recebeu da família.

Reiner durante as aulas de direç — Foto: Reiner Jesus Martins/Arquivo pessoal

O processo para obter a carteira começou ainda no ano passado. Por ser uma pessoa com deficiência, Reiner precisou passar por uma avaliação de uma junta médica do Detran, que definiu as condições e adaptações necessárias para que ele pudesse dirigir.

Segundo ele, uma das dificuldades foi encontrar uma autoescola que tivesse um veículo compatível com as adaptações indicadas. Depois de procurar, encontrou a estrutura necessária em Pará de Minas.

A primeira aula foi um momento de teste. Reiner precisava entender como executar os movimentos necessários para conduzir o veículo utilizando as adaptações. O veículo tinha câmbio automático, acelerador invertido para o lado esquerdo, comandos do painel adaptados para serem acionados com os membros inferiores e um "pomo", dispositivo instalado no volante para facilitar a direção.

Depois das aulas práticas e da prova, a aprovação veio no dia 5 de agosto.

"Logo depois que acabou o exame, que eu recebi o papelzinho escrito aprovado, eu até chorei de emoção", lembra.

Jovem que nasceu sem os braços conquista CNH após aprender a dirigir com os pés em MG — Foto: Reiner Jesus Martins/Arquivo pessoal

Apesar da conquista, Reiner acredita que o processo para que pessoas com deficiência consigam tirar a CNH ainda pode ser aprimorado.

"Acho que poderia melhorar principalmente na acessibilidade, na informação e na preparação dos profissionais. Um processo mais simples, rápido, de fácil acesso, com mais preparo dos profissionais, facilitaria para que mais pessoas com deficiência tivessem essa oportunidade e conquistassem mais autonomia", afirma.

Ele afirma que a experiência revelou dificuldades que vão além da falta de veículos adaptados. Para ele, ainda existe falta de preparo para atender pessoas com deficiência. "Muita má vontade, muito julgamento e muita questão do capacitismo ainda, principalmente na junta médica", diz.

Paixão pelo campo foi influenciada pelo pai — Foto: Reiner Jesus Martins/Arquivo pessoal

O interesse pela agronomia começou ainda na infância, por influência do pai, que trabalha com produção de leite em uma propriedade rural da família em São Tiago , no Sul de Minas.

Reiner acompanhava o trabalho do pai desde pequeno, mas sabia que algumas atividades práticas e mais pesadas seriam difíceis para ele. Durante o ensino médio, decidiu fazer um curso técnico em agropecuária no campus de Florestal da Universidade Federal de Viçosa (UFV).

Depois do curso técnico, ingressou na UFLA. Inicialmente, começou engenharia agrícola, mas decidiu mudar para agronomia. Atualmente, está no segundo período do curso.

Reiner diz que quer usar o conhecimento adquirido na universidade para ajudar o pai a melhorar a forma de trabalhar na propriedade.

"Querendo ou não, um dia o meu pai vai faltar. (...) Eu como filho, não vou jogar o trabalho dele fora, todo o esforço que ele está tendo. É uma coisa que ele sempre gostou de fazer desde novinho e é isso que ele me ensina também", diz o jovem.

Na UFLA, Reiner afirma que precisa de poucas adaptações para acompanhar o curso. Uma das principais é o uso de cadeiras específicas que permitem que ele se posicione para escrever durante as aulas sem depender de um monitor.

Reiner estuda agronomia na UFLA — Foto: Redes sociais

Nas atividades práticas em campo, porém, existem algumas limitações. Como determinadas tarefas exigem esforço físico e o uso de equipamentos de proteção, ele nem sempre consegue executá-las da mesma maneira que os colegas.

Nesses casos, ele acompanha as atividades, observa os procedimentos, faz perguntas e busca compreender a parte prática para depois aplicar o conhecimento de outras formas.

A relação com colegas e professores, segundo Reiner, é boa. Ele afirma que sempre gostou de fazer amizades e estar rodeado de pessoas.

A rotina de Reiner também passou a chamar a atenção na internet. Ele criou um perfil no TikTok e começou a publicar vídeos mostrando atividades do cotidiano, acumulando mais de 144,3 mil seguidores e 2,8 milhões de curtidas .

A ideia surgiu depois que amigos o incentivaram a mostrar como realizava as tarefas usando os pés. Ele não esperava, porém, que os vídeos alcançassem tantas pessoas.

Durante a pandemia, ele já havia experimentado produzir conteúdo para a internet. Na época, publicou um vídeo contando sua história e chegou a alcançar cerca de 10 mil seguidores rapidamente. Depois, apagou as redes sociais por ser mais novo e por não querer ficar exposto.

Reiner afirma que não começou a produzir conteúdo pensando em ganhar dinheiro. Segundo ele, o objetivo é mostrar como vive e responder à curiosidade dos seguidores. A repercussão trouxe mensagens de pessoas que dizem ter encontrado motivação ao acompanhar os vídeos.

"Eu continuo sendo o Reiner de sempre, esse menino alto astral que tem as responsabilidades, que quer vencer na vida, estudar, trabalhar, viver uma vida normal", afirma.

Reiner ministra palestras sobre sua trajetória de vida nas escolas — Foto: Redes sociais

Para Reiner, mais importante do que ser reconhecido pela deficiência é ser reconhecido pelo que faz e pela vida que constrói. Ele defende que pessoas com deficiência não sejam tratadas como incapazes ou como alguém de quem é preciso ter pena.

O jovem ainda afirma que a sociedade precisa estar mais preparada para conviver com as diferenças e compreender que pessoas com deficiência podem estudar, trabalhar, dirigir, praticar esportes, construir amizades e seguir os próprios caminhos.

"Se está na vida, não é para ter pena, não. É para viver realmente, com muita alegria, muita disposição, coragem e vontade", concluiu.

articles.title: TikTok to pay $100m, limit daily child usage in Alabama settlement
articles.summary: Alabama was set to take TikTok to trial over claims that it intentionally addicted young users.
articles.body:
TikTok and its parent company ByteDance will pay the US state of Alabama $100m (£75.45m) and make a series of changes to restrict children's usage in the state as part of a lawsuit settlement.

The deal was reached just before a jury trial was set to begin on Monday. It ends a lawsuit alleging TikTok is intentionally designed to addict children to its features, mirroring a host of lawsuits against social media platforms.

The company is now required to install a number of new safety features, including a two-hour daily usage limit for children as well as overnight and school-hour restrictions.

The changes will only apply in Alabama. It marks the platform's first settlement with a US state.

"We're very pleased," said Katherine Robertson, chief counsel in the Alabama Attorney General's office in an interview with the BBC.

She added that the state had been engaged in mediation with TikTok in the run-up to trial and that the deal they have now reached was the state's final offer.

"This is very restrictive injunctive relief that's going to require them to change a lot of the policies that we had identified as the culprits in what we call the war on childhood," Robertson said.

The new time limits and usage blocks are due to take effect immediately.

However, TikTok has up to a year to implement other changes included as part of the settlement, such as the establishment of age verification measures.

Many of the measures follow a framework established by an August settlement struck between social media rival Meta and 52 state Attorneys General.

TikTok has agreed to pay up to $300m to Alabama if conditions of the new settlement are not met. The $100m payment is due to the state within 45 days.

Other safety features demanded as part of the deal include a host of measures to allow parents to heavily moderate usage by their children, along with restrictions on some content, and new ways to verify the age of young users.

TikTok will also limit children's accounts being discovered by adults, and notify parents to any "suspicious interactions" between teen users and adult users.

A blanket ban on all cosmetic filters for children will also be put in place.

"TikTok's priority has always been fostering a safe and positive space where people can be creative, discover what they love, and connect with their community," a spokesperson for TikTok USDS said. "This builds on our commitment and core objective to continually enhance our robust safety tools to protect teens."

Earlier this year, TikTok split its business ownership , with a new group of investors taking control of operations in the US. The remainder of the business is operated out of China.

ByteDance, the parent company of TikTok in China, was also part of Friday's settlement as ByteDance remains a minority owner of the US joint venture.

articles.body: The US Supreme Court on Friday allowed the Trump administration to use a controversial federal database to help states check the citizenship status of registered voters, handing President Donald Trump a victory in his broader effort to increase federal involvement in election administration ahead of the midterm elections.The court's conservative majority lifted restrictions on the Trump administration's use of the Systematic Alien Verification for Entitlements (SAVE) programme, which allows officials to verify citizenship and immigration information.Critics have questioned the reliability of the data, warning that the system could result in US citizens being wrongly flagged or removed from voter rolls.The ruling came after a federal judge in June found the expanded use of the system illegal and said it violated Americans' privacy rights. A federal appeals court had allowed that ruling to remain in place before the Supreme Court intervened.Supreme Court limits scope of voter-roll purgesWhile allowing the administration to use the database, the Supreme Court said the National Voter Registration Act prohibits broad voter-roll purges in the weeks immediately before an election.The restriction limits the "potential impact" of Friday's decision ahead of the midterm elections.States can, however, continue checking the citizenship status of individual voters using information obtained through the federal system.The three liberal-leaning justices dissented from the decision.Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson warned that the use of the system could result in eligible voters losing their voting rights."The harm caused by burdening or disenfranchising even a few lawful voters outweighs the non-existent harm that the government experiences when it is prevented from taking an action that it likely lacks the authority to take," she wrote.What is the SAVE programme?The Department of Homeland Security's SAVE programme was created in 1986 to help government officials verify the citizenship or immigration status of people applying for public benefits.The Trump administration expanded the system's capabilities last year, allowing officials to conduct bulk searches using sensitive information from Social Security records.The administration has argued that the system is lawful and necessary to prevent non-citizens from voting.The Supreme Court ruled that a 1996 law allows the Department of Homeland Security to obtain citizenship and immigration information from federal agencies and "has an obligation to respond" to states seeking such information.Participation in the SAVE programme by individual states remains voluntary.The court also said the earlier judicial order "prevents the federal government from using the programme it believes is best suited to the task".Judge had ruled expanded system violated privacy rightsIn June, US District Judge Sparkle L Soonnan, a Biden appointee, ruled against the administration's expanded use of the system.Soonnan said the revamped programme showed that the federal government "knowingly trampled on the privacy rights" of US citizens "in a manner that threatens the sacred right to vote".A federal appeals court allowed her ruling to stand before the Supreme Court overturned the restrictions on Friday.The case has drawn opposition from voting rights organisations, which argue that errors in federal citizenship data could lead to eligible voters being wrongly targeted.The League of Women Voters, the lead plaintiff in the case, called the ruling "profoundly disappointing"."...it puts millions of Americans at risk of being unlawfully targeted by the administration's unreliable voter purge database weeks before the midterm elections," the organisation said in a statement."We will be doing everything in our power to protect Americans' voting and privacy rights by ensuring that the district court decision stands," it said.Critics point to errors in voter citizenship checksA total of 27 states currently use the SAVE system to check voter citizenship, according to the report.Critics have pointed to cases where the system has produced incorrect results.In Travis County, Texas, officials found that at least 10% of nearly 100 voters identified as non-citizens were actually US citizens, according to US media reports. Officials also indicated that the proportion could have been higher.Since Texas began checking its voter rolls through SAVE last year, only three non-citizen voters have been charged with illegally voting in the state.The examples have fuelled concerns among voting rights groups about the reliability of citizenship data and the potential consequences of acting on inaccurate records.Georgia says safeguards are in placeSome states, including Georgia, have worked with the federal government on the SAVE programme.Georgia Secretary of State Brad Raffensperger, a Republican, has publicly supported his office's work with the system and offered recommendations for improving it.Raffensperger told the BBC that his office thoroughly reviewed government-provided information before determining whether people flagged by the system were non-citizens.He said officials also interviewed some of the voters in question to verify the information."There's always guardrails in place, to make sure that we never denied the right to vote," Raffensperger said.Trump's broader push to change US election rulesThe Supreme Court ruling comes as the Trump administration pursues broader changes to the US electoral system.Since returning to the White House in January last year, Trump has sought changes involving voter eligibility and election procedures, including an effort to restrict the use of mail-in ballots that was rejected by the Supreme Court.States have also carried out voter-roll reviews.In 2024, Texas Gov. Greg Abbott announced that 1,930 people with a "voter history" had been removed from the state's electoral rolls out of nearly 18 million registered voters.The figure was far below the hundreds of thousands of non-citizen voters that Trump and the Department of Homeland Security have previously suggested could be present on voter rolls.Friday's ruling allows the federal government to continue using the SAVE system for citizenship checks, while existing federal restrictions on broad voter-roll removals close to elections remain in place.You use AI every day. articles.title: Yemen’s civil war returns and overwhelms hospitals with ‘a very dangerous situation’
articles.summary: ADEN, Yemen — Tarek al-Salami, aged 7, sat in a diaper, looking frail.
articles.body: ADEN, Yemen — Tarek al-Salami, aged 7, sat in a diaper, looking frail. Normally, the malnutrition and diarrhea that weakened his tiny frame would have been treated within a few days, but nothing is normal in Yemen anymore. Tarek’s father carried him on foot from the southwestern city of Mokha as Iran-backed rebels swept in this month, bringing a return to civil war. The boy reached a hospital two days later in the government-held city of Aden, 270 kilometers (170 miles) away but it said it had no beds. Like others, it was overwhelmed by the wounded. They finally found a therapeutic feeding center. The boy arrived in “acute crisis” after the delay in care, according to the center’s director, Dr. Arwa Atef, and he only began walking again on Wednesday, over a week later. “I swear to God, when I look at him, my heart breaks,” said his father, Mohammed al-Salami. “He looks almost lifeless.” This is how the already fragile health system in the Arab world’s poorest nation is collapsing, caught in a new front of the Iran war. The Associated Press spoke with patients, medical workers and aid groups in Yemen as medicines run short and some workers flee. A few facilities have been overtaken by the fighting. Some health centers are turning pregnant women and others in need away to focus on trauma patients. Vulnerable children are filling incubators and sharing beds. Millions of people are affected by the fighting backed by two of the Middle East’s biggest powers as Iran-backed Houthis advance against government forces supported by Saudi Arabia. Over 130,000 have fled their homes. The feeding center where Tarek and other children are recovering is struggling to cope with a rise in patients in a country where many already were hungry, Atef said. “We can’t keep up with the situation,” she said. Overwhelmed hospitals focus on the wounded Most hospitals and primary health centers affected by the escalation in fighting closed for the first 48 hours before resuming services, the United Nations said. But the Houthis have seized the Red Sea coast, including key ports for aid. “The areas with some of the highest health needs are increasingly difficult to reach,” the World Health Organization said Friday. Less than 10% of the affected health centers are fully equipped with the trauma services that wounded people need, WHO has said. With resources thin, a painful triage is underway. Fewer facilities are handling the pregnancy-related emergencies that were killing three Yemeni women every day even before the escalation, said Francesco Galtieri with the United Nations Population Fund. That’s one of the highest rates in the Arab world. “Around 2,000 pregnant women are on the move,” with over 200 expected to deliver in the next week or so, he said. Maternity wards have been converted into emergency rooms in some hospitals close to the fighting, said Hashem Osseiran, an International Committee of the Red Cross spokesperson, adding that many lack enough anesthesia drugs, oxygen supplies and sterile surgical gloves. At a hospital treating mothers and children in the government-held city of Marib, Dr. Ahmed Modhesh said they are seeing more emergency maternity cases as other city hospitals focus on the wounded. But his facility, Martyr Mohamed Hayel hospital, lacks intensive care specialists and doesn’t have enough generators to keep all departments running if the power goes out. A midwife said the number of childbirths the hospital is handling has basically doubled to about 80. One woman with an ectopic pregnancy arrived bleeding heavily, yet the under-resourced staff were still able to perform an emergency procedure to save her life, the midwife said. She spoke on condition of anonymity because she wasn’t authorized to speak with the media. Yemen’s healthcare was in trouble before the fighting Even before the escalation, hospitals in Yemen relied on limited government support and citizen donations. Some were not able to fully pay staff. Now, “we are in a very dangerous situation,” said Fahd al-Nazari, manager of the health office in Taiz province, which has received most of the newly displaced. “Within a day or two, or a week at most, we might have to close down (some facilities). In fact, some hospitals are already closed.” Three of the province’s 17 hospitals are no longer under government control. Hospitals across Taiz had received around 635 casualties, including 112 bodies, as of Thursday after the Houthis captured Mokha, al-Nazari said. They included civilians and combatants. “We’re exhausted receiving wounded people under these circumstances,” al-Nazari said. Medical supplies and fuel are running short after key supply routes between Mokha and Taiz were largely cut off, forcing convoys onto mountainous roads unsuitable for large trucks. Even before the escalation, public hospitals in the province had just one MRI machine available. At the Yemeni-Swedish Maternity and Children’s Hospital in Taiz, incubators were full and two or three children were sharing beds in the emergency room, general manager Sami al-Sharabi said. “I’m scared that the conflict would reach the hospital,” he said. “Any explosive that could hit us would destroy the hospital, as some parts of the building are already weak.” Even hospitals in Aden, where Yemen’s government is based, struggle to cope. Doctors Without Borders said more than 60 wounded people had been admitted to Al-Gamhouria hospital in a week. Many needed urgent surgery or blood transfusions. Fighters are also seeking emergency treatment At a private hospital treating rebels in the Houthi-held city of Sanaa, two medical officials last week said it was overwhelmed with hundreds of wounded. The officials spoke on condition of anonymity because of security concerns. It was not clear how many Houthi fighters have been killed or wounded overall. Few aid agencies operate in rebel-controlled areas, as the group has detained and harassed dozens of humanitarian workers. Experts say the Houthis have struggled to pay salaries to civil servants, including public sector doctors and diverted most tax revenues to their military wing. The ICRC, one of the few global agencies still able to operate in Sanaa, last week said it delivered 22 tons of badly needed medical supplies to support “overwhelmed” hospitals. There is also little information about casualties among government forces, though one government-allied group has said over 1,500 of its fighters were wounded. Some medical workers have fled the conflict, making it harder to find care. In Mokha, Doctors Without Borders said its small team was still working “despite the severe shortage of health professionals.” The charity’s deputy coordinator of operations in Yemen, Emmanuel Massart, said three other hospitals there had closed for days before resuming services. Resupplying remains a major challenge because of closed roads, Massart said. “We should not forget about Yemen,” he said. It “remains one of the worst humanitarian crises in the world.”

articles.title: Two sentenced for 2022 murder of Argentine former rugby player
articles.summary: Loik Le Priol, 32, a former soldier who fired the fatal shots, was sentenced to 26 years in jail.
articles.body:
Two men with links to the far-right have been jailed over the fatal shooting of a former Argentine international rugby player in the streets of Paris four years ago.

Federico Martin Aramburu, who played more than twenty matches for Argentina, was killed in a drive-by shooting in 2022 after an early-morning fight broke out in a bar near Boulevard Saint-Germain.

Loik Le Priol, 32, a former soldier who fired the fatal shots, was sentenced to 26 years in jail. Romain Bouvier, 35, who opened fire initially, was sentenced to 19 years in jail.

In a Paris court on Friday, Le Priol asked Aramburu's family for forgiveness as the trial concluded.

"I'm Christian like you, the pope is here today" he said, referring to Pope Leo XIV's visit to France.

"I don't know if it's a sign... [I] hope one day you can find the strength to forgive me," Le Priol continued.

Former rugby star Aramburu was 42 when he was killed. He played for Argentina 22 times, including at the 2007 World Cup in France where he scored a try against the hosts to help his country finish third.

The player also had spells at French clubs Perpignan, Biarritz and Dax before joining Glasgow Warriors in 2010.

CCTV footage reviewed during the investigation showed Aramburu and his former rugby teammate, Shaun Hegarty, sitting at a bar opposite the former soldier, Le Priol, and his friend Bouvier on 19 March 2022.

Le Priol and Bouvier were both linked to a far-right extremist group at the time, which has since dissolved.

An altercation broke out between the two groups of men, the CCTV footage showed.

As the two former Rugby players walked off towards their hotel, Le Priol and Bouvier drove around to find them and opened fire. Aramburu died at the scene, Reuters reported.

Le Priol was subsequently arrested in Hungary while attempting to cross the border ⁠into ​Ukraine. He told Hungarian police at the time he was going to Ukraine to fight.

The defence cited post-traumatic stress disorder in Le Priol's case and childhood trauma in Bouvier's case.

But in court, Le Priol was described as "animated by the will to kill".

"The narcissistic, intrusive and uncontrollable rage of Loik Le Priol ultimately led to the gratuitous killing of Mr. Aramburu," the presiding judge said.

Meanwhile, Aramburu's widow Maria asked for a verdict that would allow her and Aramburu's three children "to build their lives as adults".

articles.summary: DHAKA: Former Bangladesh PM Sheikh Hasina Friday reached out to the \"international community\", to push for release of detained Awami League members,
articles.body: DHAKA: Former Bangladesh PM Sheikh Hasina Friday reached out to the "international community", to push for release of detained Awami League members, lifting of the ban on her party's activities and withdrawal of what she described as fabricated cases, while alleging over 1,000 babies died after Muhammad Yunus' administration and its successor BNP govt failed to procure measles vaccines."International community must also support an independent international investigation" into the developments in Bangladesh, she said while virtually addressing an event on a day PM Tarique Rahman addressed UNGA. Call for the ban on Awami League to be lifted and every fabricated case to be withdrawn," she said. "To my people at home, I say this, you are not forgotten. Your pain is my pain. Your hope is my strength," said Hasina, whose camera was off.Slamming the administrations following her ouster in 2024, Hasina said, "More than 1,000 babies have died because they failed to procure measles vaccines." articles.title: Hurricane Nolo expected to bring heavy rain as it skirts Hawaii’s Big Island
articles.summary: NAALEHU, Hawaii — Hurricane Nolo is forecast to strengthen into a major hurricane in the Pacific Ocean over the weekend, unleashing intense rain, the possibility of life-threatening flash flooding, and dangerous surf for Hawaii’s Big Island.
articles.body: NAALEHU, Hawaii — Hurricane Nolo is forecast to strengthen into a major hurricane in the Pacific Ocean over the weekend, unleashing intense rain, the possibility of life-threatening flash flooding, and dangerous surf for Hawaii’s Big Island. Nolo was a Category 1 hurricane with maximum sustained winds of 105 mph when its outer rainbands began hitting Big Island Friday evening, the National Hurricane Center said. Come Saturday, hurricane conditions are possible on the island, especially in areas with steep terrain, the weather service warned. The storm was about 145 miles south of South Point, the southernmost point of the Big Island, at around 5 p.m. local time, and was moving north-northeast at 3 mph. This marks the third hurricane in less than two months to whip past Hawaii (following Lala and Lowell). The active Pacific hurricane season is likely due to a record-setting El Niño — a natural climate pattern characterized by a rise in sea surface temperatures in the eastern Pacific, and spawns more intense and frequent cyclones there. Tess Kala, a South Point resident who grew up in the area, said the back-to-back storms are a shock to locals. “Honestly, this is the first like, whoa, what happened? We had a lot of family and friends that have lived here all their lives through generations and never experienced this before,” she said. On its current path, Nolo will move slowly northward Friday night, but will remain south of Big Island through Saturday. Then, it will turn westward and move away from the island but increase in speed Saturday into Sunday, the hurricane center said. Nolo’s center will remain well south of the main Hawaiian islands, the National Hurricane Center said. But it is forecast to strengthen into a “major hurricane” — which means Category 3 or higher — this weekend and could intensify further next week, the agency said, Hawaii Gov. Josh Green said Friday that President Donald Trump approved the state’s request for an emergency declaration for Nolo to provide federal assistance for emergency protective measures across the state. Mark Peters, a resident of Naalehu in the southern Big Island for seven years, said that the damage from the recent hurricanes has not been forgotten. “It hurts me when I see friends and neighbors and people of this community that I know, and I just see it in their eyes, I hear it in their voices. We’ve been through a lot down here, and we still got a lot to go,” Peters said. “We’re just getting started with our recovery. But to have yet another big storm hit us, and potentially even bigger than the last one, it’s difficult,” he said. While he praised his community for its resilience, he said the people are still in need of basics like food and water, and many are in the process of reconstruction. “We’re talking years. This is going to be a long recovery,” Peters said Friday. He recalled driving through Waiohinu in the aftermath of Hurricane Lala and his “eyes getting wide open with all the damage, and the cars and houses moved and not where they’re supposed to be, and Waiohinu Park having buildings in the baseball field.” Kala, the South Point resident, is preparing for Nolo by “moving everything away from the houses, tying things down, making sure that everything is hosed up and taped up as best as we possibly can.” Nolo will bring periods of heavy rain that will continue across Big Island and Maui over the weekend, and could trigger life-threatening catastrophic flooding and mudslides, especially in steep terrain across eastern and southern portions of both Big Island and Maui, the hurricane center said. Nolo is forecast to dump 8 to 12 inches of rain in eastern and southern parts of Big Island, with maximum amounts up to 16 inches. Western portions of Big Island could see one to three inches of rain with maximum amounts of six inches. Meanwhile, Maui could see four to six inches, with maximum amounts of eight inches, the National Hurricane Center said. The rest of Hawaii will experience lesser rainfall totals but isolated flooding is possible. Nolo could also bring large and damaging waves along portions of Big Island’s coastline into the weekend. A hurricane watch and tropical storm warning are in effect for Hawaii County and a tropical storm watch is in effect for Maui County. A hurricane watch means that hurricane conditions are possible within 24-36 hours. A wind advisory has been issued for the rest of the state. Tropical storm force winds will reach the Big Island on Friday afternoon, with hurricane force winds possible by late evening. A high surf advisory is in effect for south and east facing shores of Big Island and east facing shores of Maui and Molokai. A high surf advisory was also issued for east facing shores of Niihau, Kauai, and Oahu beginning Friday evening. Nolo could also spawn tornadoes and large waterspouts over and near Big Island and to the right of the track of the tropical cyclone. Marlene Lenthang reported from Los Angeles and Ryan Chandler and Shanshan Dong from Naalehu.

articles.title: 'I was crying in pain': How 3 men turned teen's birthday outing at Aastha Kunj Park into horror
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: \"I was crying and was in severe pain.\" With these words, the 17-year-old survivor recounted to police the terrifying moments she endured inside
articles.body: NEW DELHI: "I was crying and was in severe pain." With these words, the 17-year-old survivor recounted to police the terrifying moments she endured inside Aastha Kunj Park Monday, when three men allegedly overpowered her, threatened her with knives and raped her after first posing as policemen."Today (Sept 22) was my birthday. I wanted to visit Kalkaji Temple. I told my friend to take me to the temple. We reached Kalkaji around 5.45pm. After that, we had darshan at the temple till around 7pm," she stated in the FIR.She said that after visiting the temple, she and her friend bought chips and a bottle of water from outside Kalkaji metro station. They then entered the park through Gate No. 7. She suggested that they sit in the park for some time, eat something and later go for darshan at Iskcon.‘I was very scared. I told them, speak to my mother’As soon as we entered through Gate No. 7 and sat on a bench near the swings and opened the packet of chips, three men, aged around 30-35 years, came from behind. As soon as they arrived, they caught hold of my friend and slapped him. When we asked who they were, they said they were policemen and asked why we had come there at that time. They said that coming there was not allowed,” she said.The men allegedly took her friend to the other side and also took away both their phones. Two of the accused then allegedly pointed towards the bushes and asked her to go there.“I was very scared. I told them, ‘Sir, ask whatever you want to ask here. Speak to my mother.’ At that time, one of the boys said, ‘Asif bhai, take out the gun,’” she said.According to her statement, the man they called Asif was wearing a purple shirt and was the most heavily built of the three. He allegedly took out a black gun from his jeans pocket and showed it to her before putting it back.The two men then allegedly took out knives and led her towards a dark area. She alleged that Asif removed her clothes and made her lie on a bench. He then allegedly told the other accused, “Hemu, keep watch so that no one comes from this side.”According to the statement, Asif then allegedly sexually assaulted her while holding a knife to her neck. “I was crying and was in severe pain,” she told police. She alleged that after the assault, Asif removed the condom and threw it near the bench before calling Hemu. “Hemu, you come. Till then I will go to Deepu.”Hemu allegedly took her to another nearby bench and assaulted her while holding a knife to her neck, the statement said. The third accused, whom the other two allegedly called Deepu, then came and allegedly assaulted her while also holding a knife to her neck.After the assault, the accused allegedly asked her to quickly put on her clothes.“They gave me only my T-shirt and jeans. They did not give me my undergarment. I put on my clothes and then they brought my friend to me as well,” she told police.TOI had earlier reported that the accused’s nicknames, clothes and physical descriptions provided by the survivor became key clues for police in identifying the trio. Cops had also recovered a used condom from the spot.The accused allegedly returned their phones and threatened to kill them if they did not leave immediately or told anyone about the incident. They then allegedly took the two out of Aastha Kunj Park.“I told my friend about the incident of rape committed against me by the three boys. My friend then made a PCR call. articles.title: Parents, think twice before serving these breakfast foods to your child before school
articles.summary: The toughest question parents across the world battle with every morning is what to serve my child for breakfast.
articles.body: The toughest question parents across the world battle with every morning is what to serve my child for breakfast. Amidst the hustle and bustle of trying to get to school on time, the most important meal of the day often gets neglected. What children eat before school can influence how long they stay full and feel energised. The first meal of the day can also affect their concentration in class .The problem is not sugar or calories. It is the larger design of the meal: whether it contains protein, fibre, useful fats and micronutrients; whether it is filling enough; and whether it has been engineered to be eaten quickly instead of slowly and mindfully.On this note, let’s have a look at some of the best breakfasts for kids:Sugary breakfast cerealsA cereal bowl seems like the easiest option for breakfast: add milk, pour your cereal and you are done. But more and more children's cereals are closer to dessert than to a nutritious meal. They may provide energy quickly because some cereals are high on sugar and low on protein and fibre. Because not all children's cereals are high in sugar or low in protein/fibre. So before you buy any cereal, do check the back of the packet for its nutritional value.That is why nutritionist Rujuta Diwekar has repeatedly advised parents through social media posts to avoid making packaged and processed food the default breakfast. She advises a simple alternative: fresh food like poha, upma, idli, dosa, paratha or dalia.Juice, even when it says “real fruit”Fruit juice is often presented as a healthy shortcut. But juice removes much of the fiber that makes whole fruit filling, and it is easy to drink a large amount of sugar in a few minutes.The World Health Organisation classifies sugars naturally present in fruit juice and fruit-juice concentrates as free sugars, and recommends limiting free-sugar intake across the life course. It also notes that sugar-sweetened drinks do not create the same feeling of fullness as solid food.Water, milk, or whole fruit alongside a proper meal is usually a more useful morning habit. If a child likes juice, it need not become forbidden forever; it simply should not replace a full breakfast every day.Biscuits, toast and jam as the entire mealTwo biscuits or slices of white toast with jam may solve a time problem, but they do not solve a nutrition problem. This combination is predominantly refined carbohydrate and sugar, with little protein and limited fibre.Pooja Makhija, celebrity nutritionist, has warned against beginning the day with sweet combinations such as bread-jam, biscuit, corn flakes, and juice, arguing that a sweet-heavy breakfast can produce a sharper rise in blood sugar than a more balanced meal and be addictive. A more complete option could be toast with egg, paneer, peanut butter or hummus, plus fruit.Flavoured milk and malted drinksFlavoured milk, chocolate powders and malt-based drinks are often marketed as nourishment in a glass. Some may contain useful nutrients, but they can also add sugar and encourage children to reject plain milk or water.In her book, Notes For Healthy Kids, Rujuta Diwekar advises, “If you can only drink milk by masking its taste, then don't have it.” Often the chocolate powders, claiming to make your child taller and stronger, are filled with sugar, and a high-sugar breakfast causes more harm than good.Instant noodles and packaged savoury snacksInstant noodles, chips and packaged savoury snacks can be high in sodium and refined carbohydrates while providing little protein or fibre.They are also easy to eat while distracted, in a car or on the way to school. Children may finish the food without registering whether they are full. A meal that is eaten in three minutes from a packet is not equivalent to a meal that contains several food groups and is eaten with some attention.This does not mean that noodles have to be completely eliminated. They are okay if served occasionally, adding vegetables, paneer or tofu to make the meal more substantial.Coffee, tea and energy drinksChildren do not need caffeine to compensate for inadequate sleep, early school timings or an overloaded schedule. Tea and coffee can also suppress appetite, meaning a child may consume a stimulant instead of eating a proper breakfast.Energy drinks are particularly unsuitable for children because they may combine caffeine with large amounts of sugar or other stimulants. They are not a breakfast, a study aid or a safe substitute for sleep.The morning routine should address the underlying issue: an earlier bedtime, prepared food or a more realistic school schedule; rather than make a child dependent on stimulation.The real breakfast testA useful test is not, “Does this food contain sugar?” Almost every normal diet can include some sugar. The better questions are:Does the meal contain a source of protein?Is there fibre from fruit, vegetables, pulses or whole grains?Will it keep the child reasonably satisfied until the next eating opportunity?Is the drink adding nourishment, or merely sweetness?Can the child eat it without rushing or using a screen?Is this an occasional convenience or the default breakfast every morning?Children should not be frightened away from food, and parents should not be made to feel guilty about every rushed morning. The goal is to stop treating highly processed, sweet or stimulant-heavy products as the natural starting point for a school day.A banana with milk and nuts, an egg with roti, vegetable poha, idli with sambar, dal chilla with curd or leftover dal and rice can all be perfectly reasonable breakfasts. The best morning meal is the one that gives a child nourishment, steadier energy and a realistic chance of making it through the school day without breakfast becoming another source of stress for the parents.You use AI every day. articles.title: British company turns plasterboard waste into tiles with more than 95% recycled content, without kiln firing
articles.summary: A Manchester-based materials company is developing tiles that avoid the high-temperature kiln firing normally associated with ceramic manufacturing.
articles.body: A Manchester-based materials company is developing tiles that avoid the high-temperature kiln firing normally associated with ceramic manufacturing. DeKiln's BioSintering technology uses waste gypsum plaster, a material commonly recovered from plasterboard, together with a bio-based binder to produce its Eralith tiles. DeKiln says the tiles contain more than 95% recycled content and are cured at low temperatures rather than fired in a kiln. The company describes conventional ceramic production as requiring kiln temperatures of roughly 850°C to 1,250°C and says firing and drying account for about 80% of the ceramics industry's emissions. Its current product information states that BioSintering can reduce energy consumption by up to 90% compared with conventional ceramic manufacturing. The technology is still being scaled for industrial production, however, so these environmental figures should be understood as reported comparisons rather than evidence that the process has already replaced conventional tile manufacturing at large scale.How recycled gypsum replaces conventional tile materialsThe material at the centre of the process is waste gypsum plaster, or calcium sulphate dihydrate, which can be recovered from plasterboard and other construction waste. DeKiln estimates that the UK produces about 980,000 tonnes of plasterboard waste each year and says its process can turn this waste stream into a useful manufacturing input. The company first processes the waste gypsum into a base material with properties suitable for tile production. It then combines the recycled material with a proprietary bio-based active ingredient to create a precursor designed to behave similarly to conventional ceramic tile powder. DeKiln says its Eralith tiles currently contain more than 95% recycled gypsum plaster or recycled content, depending on the product information used, while its broader technology pages describe the recycled material as primarily waste gypsum plaster combined with a bio-based ingredient. The important point is that the process replaces most of the conventional mineral feedstock with recovered material rather than relying primarily on newly extracted raw materials.Tiles are pressed normally, but do not go through a kilnAfter the recycled material and binder are mixed, the precursor is compressed using standard tile presses. This allows the company to use familiar manufacturing equipment rather than requiring a completely different production system. The major difference comes after pressing: instead of sending the formed tiles into a high-temperature kiln, BioSintering uses a low-temperature curing stage. DeKiln's technology page describes curing at 30°C, while its 2026 partnership announcement with Johnson Tiles describes the tiles being hardened on a drying rack at 35°C. DeKiln's newer manufacturing information more broadly describes its process as operating 90 °C below, reflecting different stages or configurations of the technology as it is being developed. The company has therefore demonstrated a kiln-free route to hardening its ceramic-like tiles, but the exact curing temperature can vary according to the particular process description. In May 2026, DeKiln announced a pilot manufacturing project with Johnson Tiles in Stoke-on-Trent to help scale the technology.The company reports major reductions in emissions and energy useDeKiln says its BioSintering process produces 94% lower carbon dioxide emissions and 99% lower particulate air pollution than conventional ceramic tiles. Its current product information says these figures are supported by an independent life-cycle assessment, which gives the Eralith tiles a reported global-warming potential of 0.81 kilograms of CO₂-equivalent per square metre. DeKiln also reports energy savings of up to 90%, attributing much of the reduction to eliminating the high-temperature firing stage. The company says its tiles can achieve flexural strength of up to 25 megapascals, compared with a 12-megapascal minimum requirement it cites for ceramic tiles, and reports water absorption below 10%. These performance figures describe the company's current Eralith products and should not be interpreted as meaning that every possible application has already been certified. DeKiln currently recommends the tiles for indoor wall applications in dry environments, while continuing to develop their range of uses and certifications.The technology is now moving from development towards industrial scaleBioSintering is designed to work with conventional tile manufacturing equipment, with DeKiln saying producers can use existing presses and other equipment without the kiln, requiring only limited modifications and retraining. The company has worked with organisations including the University of Manchester, Teamwork Italy and Johnson Tiles, while its technology has received support through UK innovation and engineering programmes. In 2025, DeKiln received funding through the Royce Industrial Collaboration Programme for the SPARK project, which aimed to move BioSintering from laboratory batch production towards pre-pilot-scale manufacturing. In 2026, the company announced a partnership with Johnson Tiles to establish a pilot manufacturing site in Stoke-on-Trent. The Royal Academy of Engineering has also selected DeKiln founder Aled Roberts as a 2026 Green Future Fellow, with the Academy describing the technology as producing tiles from more than 98% recycled gypsum without kiln firing. The developments show that DeKiln is moving beyond laboratory research, but the company is still working through the scale-up process needed for widespread industrial production.You use AI every day. articles.title: OpenAI says its AI agents bypassed security controls on US government websites
articles.summary: OpenAI has disclosed that its AI agents interacted with the websites of dozens of organisations in unintended ways, with some agents bypassing security
articles.body: OpenAI has disclosed that its AI agents interacted with the websites of dozens of organisations in unintended ways, with some agents bypassing security controls while trying to access information. The affected organisations included US government agencies such as the Securities and Exchange Commission and Census Bureau.According to the BBC, citing OpenAI, some agents were trying to find authoritative public information, while others went beyond their intended behaviour by bypassing website security measures or using tools in unintended ways.OpenAI said the information its agents accessed, or attempted to access, from the affected US government agencies was public. In the case of the Census Bureau, the company said its agents used tools meant for software developers to obtain information.OpenAI described some of the incidents as cases of "misalignment", meaning the AI behaved in a way that its developers did not intend.The company also identified at least 53 incidents in which AI agents took images from ChatGPT user activity and transferred them elsewhere. OpenAI said the users had opted in to allow their data to be used for model training, but acknowledged that transferring the images was not an appropriate use of the data.The disclosures follow a July incident involving AI developer platform Hugging Face, where OpenAI said a swarm of its AI agents hacked the platform without being prompted to do so. The incident led OpenAI to begin a broader review of its agents' activities.OpenAI said it is reviewing the activity month by month and that the investigation could take months. The company said most cases identified so far were low severity, with limited or no evidence of meaningful impact.The issue has also emerged outside the United States. Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese recently said an OpenAI agent had accessed non-public files on a government-run healthcare website.The incidents highlight concerns over increasingly autonomous AI agents, which can browse websites, use software tools and take actions on behalf of users. Such systems can sometimes pursue a legitimate task through methods their developers did not intend.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Yemeni leader urges public to enlist, offers amnesty to Houthi defectors
articles.summary: Rashad al-Alimi pledges amnesty for Houthi defectors in first speech since losing ground on the western Red Sea coast.
articles.body:
The head of Yemen’s governing body has called on people to mobilise and join the Saudi-backed armed forces as it seeks to counter advances made by the Houthis towards the critical Bab al-Mandeb strait.

The Yemeni Presidential Leadership Council chair Rashad al-Alimi also pledged on Friday to pardon any Houthi fighter who defects to the government forces in his first speech since the government forces were routed from the western Red Sea coast by the rebel group.

“I call on the sons of our great people to engage in a general mobilisation and national mobilisation to rally around their armed and security forces, join their ranks through official channels, and contribute each from their respective position in whatever way they can,” he said in a recorded speech.

Al-Alimi said the internationally recognised government aims to restore control over Sana’a, the capital, which the Houthis seized in 2014. His speech marks the 64th anniversary of the military coup ousting the monarchy that ruled northern Yemen, prompting the civil war in 1962.

“Our objective is clear to everyone both at home and abroad: to restore state institutions and exercise their sovereignty over the entire country, including Sana’a,” Al-Alimi said.

Earlier on Friday, the military chiefs of staff of Saudi Arabia , Turkiye and Pakistan held their first meeting on the trilateral defence agreement, the Mecca Pact, amid the Houthis’ ongoing attacks on the kingdom.

Al-Alimi said the amnesty is effective immediately and will include those who leave the Houthi group, provided that the pardon is issued in accordance with proper constitutional and legal procedures.

On Saturday, the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen said on X that its air defence systems intercepted one ballistic missile headed towards Saudi Arabia’s Khamis Mushait launched by the Houthis and two drones headed towards Riyadh.

articles.title: Saudi Arabia has not ruled out developing nuclear weapons, classified US assessment warns
articles.summary: The US Congress has reportedly received a classified intelligence assessment warning that Saudi Arabia has not ruled out developing a nuclear weapons
articles.body: The US Congress has reportedly received a classified intelligence assessment warning that Saudi Arabia has not ruled out developing a nuclear weapons programme, according to a report by The Washington Post.The assessment comes after Washington and Riyadh confirmed in July that they had reached an agreement that could potentially allow Saudi Arabia to develop uranium enrichment capabilities as part of its civilian nuclear programme.The agreement has raised concerns among US lawmakers from both parties and Israeli officials over the possibility that Saudi Arabia could eventually use the technology to develop nuclear weapons. However, the Republican-controlled US legislature does not appear likely to block its implementation.A group of Democratic senators, led by Massachusetts Senator Ed Markey and Oregon Senator Jeff Merkley, wrote to Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Friday, warning that the departure from established precedent could set in motion a process “that is all but certain to allow Riyadh to acquire the means to enrich uranium and possibly develop nuclear weapons.”Merkley called the situation “bogus as hell”, arguing that Saudi Arabia’s demands indicated that its nuclear programme could extend beyond civilian purposes.“If they’ve given up the intent to develop a nuclear weapon, then they’d give up domestic enrichment and reprocessing power, right? They’d accept massive inspections from the IAEA,” he said.Markey linked his concerns to the ongoing war with Iran, noting that Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman had previously warned that Riyadh would seek to develop a nuclear bomb if Tehran did so.“It is very clear that as this war in Iran continues to unfold, that the Iranians are going to fiercely defend their ability to develop a nuclear weapons program, and as a result, any action that we take in Saudi Arabia will only further accelerate a fallout nuclear arms race in the region,” Markey said.The Democratic senators’ letter also criticised Trump administration officials whom they said stood to benefit from the agreement.“Jared Kushner, for example, accepted a $2 billion investment from a Saudi sovereign wealth fund after leaving the White House at the end of the first Trump Administration,” the report said.“Westinghouse Electric, meanwhile, stands to make tens of billions of dollars if this agreement moves forward. Westinghouse’s majority owner is closely associated with Newmark, the real estate firm run and owned in part by the sons of Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick.”Under the agreement, US businesses will participate in developing nuclear power projects in Saudi Arabia, a move expected to boost the US nuclear power industry and strengthen ties between the two countries. The 30-year agreement gives US companies a central role in developing Saudi Arabia’s civilian nuclear infrastructure, largely excluding foreign competitors.Saudi Arabia will be allowed to enrich uranium to nearly 20 per cent under the agreement, well below the level required to make a nuclear weapon, as cited by The New York Times. However, uranium enriched to that level could be further enriched to weapons-grade material within a relatively short period.The agreement comes against the backdrop of wider concerns over a potential nuclear arms race in the Middle East. Israel is an undeclared nuclear power, while Iran has long pursued uranium enrichment, one of the reasons the United States attacked Iran in February.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.summary: US President Donald Trump on Friday posted a map on Truth Social depicting the Strait of Hormuz as “Trump Strait.” This comes after Trump reportedly
articles.body: US President Donald Trump on Friday posted a map on Truth Social depicting the Strait of Hormuz as “Trump Strait.”This comes after Trump reportedly rejected Iran’s seven-day framework offer for reopening the strait and resuming negotiations over its nuclear programme.According to The Washington Post, Trump vowed that Iran would never acquire a nuclear bomb, expressed scepticism that Tehran would meet his demands and said a renewed US bombing campaign remained likely.Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi had earlier said normal maritime passage through the Strait of Hormuz could be restored within seven days if Washington accepted Tehran’s conditions.Under the proposal, the US would lift its naval blockade of Iranian ports, waive sanctions on Iranian oil sales and observe a ceasefire that includes Lebanon.“If the necessary conditions are met, the strait can be reopened, a normal maritime passage restored within seven days. The choice now rests with the United States,” Araghchi said.“The seven-day timeline will start as soon as the United States accepts this plan,” he added.This is not the first time Trump has floated the idea of US control over the Strait of Hormuz. In August, he posted a map suggesting the waterway could become “new US territory”.Trump had also described the idea of declaring Hormuz a US territory as a “great idea”, arguing that Washington already controlled the strait through its blockade.“I think it's a great idea. I mean, we control it with the blockade. I like the idea of declaring it a territory. We have total control over the Strait,” Trump said.He added that Iran could disrupt shipping by placing mines in the water, but claimed the US blockade had been effective.The Strait of Hormuz has emerged as one of Iran’s main sources of leverage in its confrontation with Washington.Before the war, about a fifth of the world's traded oil and gas passed through the strategic waterway, according to the Washington Post report. Disruptions to shipping have affected energy markets and increased pressure on the Trump administration ahead of the US midterm elections.Iran's proposal directly linked the reopening of the waterway to the lifting of the US blockade, sanctions relief and a renewed diplomatic process over its nuclear programme.You use AI every day. articles.title: Reigning champion Indiana Hoosiers survive major scare from Northwestern in Big Ten opener
articles.summary: The National Champion Indiana Hoosiers barely survived Northwestern as penalties and Turbo Richard's injury nearly derailed their Big Ten opener.
articles.body: The reigning National Champion Indiana Hoosiers haven't been tested much this season, and boy, did they ever get a test on Friday night. Despite being three-touchdown favorites, the Hoosiers found themselves battling the Northwestern Wildcats to the very end, eking out a 29-23 win at home. Coming into Friday night's game, the Hoosiers — despite getting off to a 3-0 start on the heels of a title — had dealt with one big criticism dogging them this season. Slow starts. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Head coach Curt Cignetti had to field questions about his team's play early in games against easier opponents. So, there was a lot of focus on whether or not that trend would continue as the Big Ten schedule got underway against the Wildcats. Well, the answer was... kind of? The Hoosiers opened the game with a 15-play, 67-yard drive that ate up around half of the opening quarter. However, the slow-start bug showed up again when a drive that should’ve ended with points on the board was instead capped by a huge defensive play from Northwestern. The Indiana defense managed to bail out the boys on the other side of the ball when Northwestern QB Aidan Chiles fumbled a snap before getting brought down in his own end zone for a safety. The Hoosiers battled through an unusual first half with an offense that looked a little disjointed at times and more penalties than you typically see out of them. ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW! Worse, they suffered a big blow later in the half when running back Turbo Richard was hit late after going out of bounds and went straight to the locker room. There was no call on the play, which made a call against Indiana on a similar play moments later very unpopular with the folks at Memorial Stadium. Indiana tacked on a touchdown and extra point to take a 12-0 lead to the locker room at the half; of course, it didn't hurt that Northwestern rushed for -5 yards through thirty minutes. But just over halfway through the third quarter, Northwestern paid their first visit to the red zone and managed to get rid of that goose egg. Chiles wrapped up that drive, despite suffering what sure appeared to be a dislocated finger, and led the Wildcats to the first points Indiana had allowed since their season opener. And the Wildcats weren't done, with Chiles hitting Griffin Wilde in the back of the end zone at the start of the fourth quarter for an unbelievable touchdown. Northwestern head coach David Braun opted to go for two and try to tie it up, but the Hoosiers thwarted them on their first and then their second attempts after a penalty. Indiana answered back with a scoring drive of their own, with Lee Beebe Jr. — who handled most of the legwork after Richard's exit — putting the Hoosiers in the red zone with a 39-yard carry, before punching it in for a touchdown two plays later. Penalties were a story for Indiana, who averaged just three penalties per game so far this season, but wound up with nearly triple that. Some were costly too, including a holding penalty that set the Wildcats up on the Indiana 4-yardline, and a few plays later Chiles took matters into his own hands. Beebe threw down another huge play to put the Hoosiers back in scoring position. It looked like the Wildcats were on the cusp of another goal-line stand, but a costly defensive pass interference penalty gave Indiana a fresh set of downs, with QB Josh Hoover finding the end zone on a keeper that fooled just about everyone in the building. Northwestern tacked on a field goal on the ensuing drive, but Indiana managed to recover their attempt at an onside kick. That slow start habit is still going to be a talking point, as it let Northwestern stay in the game. And while the injury to Richard is a big concern, Beebe's play — he finished with 203 rushing yards — was a major bright spot. articles.title: PAM wins big in Morocco parliament elections but falls short of majority
articles.summary: The next government will steer Morocco’s 2030 World Cup preparations amid public frustration over local economy.
articles.body:
Morocco’s Authenticity and Modernity Party (PAM) has won the most seats in the country’s parliamentary election.

The monarchy-aligned PAM, part of the ruling coalition, took 97 of the 395 seats in the House of Representatives, Morocco’s lower house of parliament, according to final results announced by the Ministry of Interior on Friday.

Under Morocco’s constitution, King Mohammed VI must appoint a prime minister from the party that wins the most seats, but PAM fell well short of the 198 seats needed for an outright majority and will need to build a coalition with other parties to govern.

PAM, founded in 2008 by Fouad Ali El Himma, a friend of the king, has long been seen as a counterweight to the Justice and Development Party (PJD), a moderate Islamist party that led the government for a decade before its parliamentary seats collapsed to 13 in 2021.

The PJD staged a striking comeback this time, quadrupling its seats to 54.

A longstanding rivalry with PAM makes a coalition between the two parties unlikely. The PJD has said it will remain in opposition, leaving PAM expected to turn instead to the monarchist Istiqlal party, which came third, and other parties to form a governing majority.

PAM’s senior coalition partner, the National Rally of Independents (RNI), lost significant ground, falling from 102 seats to 66.

Only 38 percent of Morocco’s 15.8 million registered voters cast ballots, the second-lowest turnout since King Mohammed VI ascended to the throne in 1999, after a record-low 37 percent in 2007, and sharply down from the roughly 51 percent recorded in 2021.

Analysts attribute the low number to widespread disengagement following youth-led protests last year over jobs, healthcare and education, and deadly mass attempts by migrants to reach Spain’s North African enclave of Ceuta in July.

Potential candidates for prime minister include PAM members Fouzi Lekjaa, head of Morocco’s football federation and budget minister, and Fatima Ezzahra Mansouri, a PAM member who currently serves as mayor of Marrakech as well as minister of national planning, urban planning, housing and urban policy. Mansouri would become Morocco’s first woman to hold the post if chosen.

The incoming government will oversee billions of dollars in investment as Morocco prepares to cohost the 2030 World Cup alongside Spain and Portugal.

articles.title: Girl or boy? Parents who have these children are among the world’s happiest, says new study
articles.summary: Does having a daughter or a son make a difference to how happy parents feel? A new study from China has found an interesting pattern.
articles.body: Does having a daughter or a son make a difference to how happy parents feel? A new study from China has found an interesting pattern. Parents who had only daughters reported higher levels of happiness than those who had only sons. The association was particularly strong among parents with ‘two daughters,’ according to the study. But the researchers are careful about what the finding means. The study does not show that having daughters causes parents to be happier. Researchers Zhong Fei and Wenqin Jin examined six waves of data from the Chinese General Social Survey collected between 2012 and 2021. The study looked at the relationship between parenthood, the number of children, the gender composition of children and reported happiness.Parents with daughters reported higher happinessThe study found that parents with only daughters tended to report higher happiness than parents with only sons. Among different combinations of children, the association was strongest for parents with two daughters. The pattern was not the same across every group. According to the researchers, the association between having all-female children and higher reported happiness was strongest among middle-aged parents. It also varied according to factors such as whether parents lived in urban or rural areas and their gender.This is not the first research to examine the relationship between children's gender and parents' happiness in China. A 2021 study published in the Chinese Journal of Sociology, also examined children's gender composition alongside other aspects of family life and happiness. That study found a slightly higher happiness score among parents with only daughters compared with parents with only sons, although the difference was not statistically significant in that analysis.Why might daughters be linked with higher happiness?The researchers discuss several possible explanations related to family relationships and China's social context, but these should not be treated as proven causes. Earlier research has examined how adult children affect the well-being of Chinese parents. A 2021 study found that children's characteristics, including their education and marital status, were associated with parents' happiness, and that these relationships could change at different stages of life.Research on older adults in China has also found differences in the kinds of support associated with sons and daughters. One study using data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study found that older adults with only daughters were more similar to those with children of both sexes than to those with only sons when it came to receiving economic support.The study has an important limitationThe most important point is that this was an observational study based on survey data. It found associations between children's number or gender composition and parents' reported happiness; it did not prove cause and effect. In other words, the research cannot establish that having two daughters makes a parent happier. There may be many other factors affecting happiness, including income, health, marriage, location, family relationships and the kind of support parents receive from their adult children.There is also a cultural limitation. The study used data from China, so its findings cannot automatically be applied to parents in India, the US, Europe or other countries. Family roles, expectations around sons and daughters and relationships between parents and adult children differ considerably between societies.So, are parents of daughters happier? Well, the study provides an interesting answer, but not a universal one.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ testGet the latest Lifestyle News and more. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: In 2024, Allen Treibitz paid $50 for a painting at a Hamptons barn sale; months later it was authenticated as Emily Carr’s 1912 Masset, Q.C.I. and sold at a Toronto auction for C$290,000
articles.summary: A dusty barn sale in the Hamptons is not where most people expect to encounter a significant work of Canadian art.
articles.body: A dusty barn sale in the Hamptons is not where most people expect to encounter a significant work of Canadian art. Yet that is exactly where New York-based art dealer Allen Treibitz found a painting that would eventually sell for hundreds of thousands of Canadian dollars. Bought for just $50, the canvas was later authenticated as a 1912 work by Emily Carr, one of Canada's most celebrated artists. The discovery turned an overlooked painting into one of the more remarkable bargain finds to reach the auction market in 2024, states Canadian Press report.An unexpected find in the HamptonsTreibitz came across the signed canvas while browsing a barn sale in the Hamptons. At the time, he was not particularly familiar with Carr or the significance of her work, but something about the painting stood out among the objects surrounding it. After taking the painting home, he began researching it online and eventually contacted Heffel Fine Art Auction House in Vancouver. Specialists examined the work and determined that it was an authentic Emily Carr painting.The discovery was eventually identified as Masset, Q.C.I., an oil on canvas measuring approximately 41 by 33 centimetres, adds the online report.A glimpse of Haida GwaiiPainted in 1912, Masset, Q.C.I. depicts an Indigenous memorial post topped with a carved grizzly bear in Masset, a village on British Columbia's Haida Gwaii archipelago, historically known as the Queen Charlotte Islands. The work dates from an important period in Carr's career, when she was documenting landscapes and Indigenous subjects in British Columbia. Born in Victoria to British immigrant parents, Carr later became closely associated with the Canadian art movement surrounding the Group of Seven. The painting also carried clues to its earlier history. An inscription on the reverse refers to an address on Boulevard Montparnasse in Paris, believed to connect to Carr's period of study in France around 1910 and 1911.From a barn to the auction blockAccording to the report, the painting's provenance offered another intriguing chapter. It is believed to have been given by Carr to her friends Nell Cozier and her husband during the 1930s. The couple, originally from Victoria, later moved to the Hamptons to work on a large estate, where the painting apparently remained in a barn for decades. When Heffel announced the work for its November 20, 2024 Toronto auction, the auction house placed an estimate of C$100,000 to C$200,000 on it. Competitive bidding pushed the hammer price to C$290,000, comfortably above the high estimate. Heffel's records put the final price, including fees, at C$349,250, the report mentions.Image Courtesy: PeopleYou use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.
